name: Plate-Loaded Machine Row — Low Row
description: The plate-loaded low row machine targets the lower lats and mid-back through a horizontal pulling path at approximately waist height. The low cable angle maximizes latissimus dorsi engagement compared to a high row configuration. The chest-supported position allows trainees to train to muscular failure safely without lower back fatigue limiting back muscle training.

execution.starting_position: Sit facing the machine with the chest on the pad. Set the seat so the handles are at approximately waist-to-lower-chest height. Grip the handles with arms fully extended.
execution.setup_instructions: Load the machine with appropriate weight. The low angle maximizes lat stretch at the start.
steps: Step 1: Sit with chest on the support pad, arms fully extended gripping the handles.
Step 2: Retract the scapulae and pull the handles toward the lower chest or abdomen.
Step 3: Keep the elbows close to the torso to maximize lat activation.
Step 4: Squeeze the lats at peak contraction.
Step 5: Return under control to full extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the row, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows too wide, shifting to a rhomboid-dominant movement
Using too much weight, reducing range of motion
safety_considerations: Check chest pad height before loading heavy — improper fit causes shoulder discomfort
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at the start to handles at lower ribcage level at the finish.
coaching_cues: Think about pulling the elbows to your pockets
Full stretch at the start of every rep
